analysis.title: CIO Weekly Commentary: Emerging opportunities to diversify AI concentration
key_insights: October CPI came in hotter than expected. Headline rose 0.4% and core 0.3% on the month, both 0.1 point above consensus.
Breadth of the core increase was wide. Nearly 60% of core items rose at an annualized pace above 3% in October, and 3.7% over the past three months (Piper Sandler).
October PPI rose 0.3% on the month, slightly below expectations. Year-over-year PPI was 6.5%, the highest annual rate since November 2022.
Atlanta Fed Core Sticky CPI is at 3.1% year over year. Nuveen says this adds to the debate over a Fed rate hike.
Nuveen expects a 25 bp Fed hike at the December meeting, with a possible additional 25 bp hike in 2027.

Oil prices have declined on hopes of a diplomatic resolution to the U.S.-Iran conflict. Nuveen says lower oil may not quickly reduce consumer inflation because businesses are still absorbing earlier price increases.
Nuveen flags AI infrastructure spending as a possible driver of higher interest rates (capital demand) and higher inflation (input costs for semiconductors and equipment).
Nuveen suggests adding emerging markets debt to diversify away from AI concentration. The U.S. is 40% of the Bloomberg Global Aggregate Index.
EM debt spans over 70 countries and more than 12 corporate sectors. South Korea and Taiwan are 4% and 2% of the corporate EM index, and neither is in JPMorgan's sovereign or local EM indexes.

The yield premium on local-currency EM debt over U.S. bonds has compressed since the 2007-2009 crisis, which Nuveen reads as better EM policymaking. EM flows stayed resilient through the energy shock from the U.S.-Iran conflict.
Côte d'Ivoire is projected to grow 6% or more in 2026 and 2027 as its exports diversify beyond cocoa.
Week ahead: October retail sales on Tuesday, the Fed's October meeting minutes on Wednesday, and the final November University of Michigan sentiment print on Friday.

macro_indicators.interpretation: One-tenth above consensus. Adds to the case for a Fed hike.
One-tenth above consensus. Nearly 60% of core items rose at an annualized pace above 3%.
Slightly below expectations on the month.
Sticky prices respond to persistent pressures and carry more weight in long-term inflation expectations. Adds to the rate hike debate.
Nuveen's expectation. One more 25 bp hike is possible in 2027.
Nuveen sees this as a possibility, not a base case.

trade_ideas.description: Add emerging markets debt exposure to diversify away from AI concentration in portfolios
trade_ideas.rationale: U.S. risk is 40% of the Bloomberg Global Aggregate, EM debt is less correlated with technology, and EM policy buffers have improved.

risk_factors: Sticky core inflation could push the Fed to hike.
AI infrastructure spending could raise interest rates and input costs.
Lower oil prices may not quickly lower consumer inflation.
The Fed minutes could show a shift from the gradual approach to policy changes.
EM investments carry currency, political, liquidity and credit risks.
geopolitical: U.S.-Iran conflict: hopes of a diplomatic resolution have pushed oil lower. The earlier energy shock did not stop EM investment flows.

tension_points.bull_case: Oil is falling on hopes of a U.S.-Iran diplomatic resolution, which could eventually ease energy-related inflation.
tension_points.bear_case: Core CPI breadth is wide and Core Sticky CPI is 3.1%. Lower oil may not quickly reduce consumer inflation because businesses are still absorbing earlier price increases.
tension_points.what_invalidates: The Fed minutes on Wednesday showing a shift away from the gradual approach to policy changes.
